meta.title: beautifulios — Offline Outbox (GRDB) and its Drain Triggers

cards.title: The outbox is a table, not a hope
items: the mutation and its outbox row are written in one GRDB transaction — the app can be killed between them and neither is lost
each row carries an idempotency key, so a retry after a timeout does not archive twice
the row is persisted before the UI claims success: a fire-and-forget mutation with no rollback is a review finding
GRDB runs in WAL; migrations are code-defined and tested against fixtures of every released version

cards.title: What drains it
items: three triggers: the network reconnects, the app returns to the foreground, and a background task runs while the app is suspended
the drain is bounded — a batch of pending rows goes out per pass, and the rest stay queued
a failed row is retried with backoff and, once the attempts are exhausted, lands in a dead-letter view a human can act on
the drain runs off the main actor; a GRDB query on the main actor is a review finding

cards.title: The server resolves conflicts
items: a conflict is resolved by the server: the local pending change is rejected visibly, never silently overwritten
the rejected mutation returns to the screen as a rendered state so the user sees that their change did not land
sign out or a tenant switch clears the outbox with the rest of the user data
